ar-1f239c4c.stem: At which joints do inversion and eversion of the foot mainly occur?
ar-1f239c4c.explanation: The talocrural joint is a hinge and allows dorsiflexion–plantarflexion. Inversion–eversion occurs below the talus, at the subtalar (talocalcaneal) and talocalcaneonavicular joints, with a small part at the transverse tarsal (Chopart) joint.

ar-e770222c.stem: In which position is the ankle (talocrural) joint most stable, and why?
options: In inversion, because the lateral ligaments are taut.
In dorsiflexion, because the trochlea of the talus is wider in front and locks firmly between the malleoli.
In plantarflexion, because the deltoid ligament is tautest.
In plantarflexion, because the malleoli fully grip the talus.
In neutral, because the capsule is most lax.
ar-e770222c.explanation: The trochlea of the talus is wide in front and narrow behind. In dorsiflexion the wide front part wedges between the malleoli and the joint is stable. In plantarflexion the narrow part lies in the mortise and the joint loosens; this is why sprains mostly occur in plantarflexion.

ar-fe165037.stem: Which statement about the sacroiliac joint is true?
options: It is a ball-and-socket joint allowing a wide range of movement.
It is a mixed joint: synovial in front, joined behind by strong interosseous ligaments.
It is not affected in ankylosing spondylitis.
It lies between the coccyx and the ilium.
It is an entirely fibrous joint.
ar-fe165037.explanation: The part of the sacroiliac joint between the auricular surfaces is synovial; behind it are the interosseous sacroiliac ligaments, among the strongest in the body. It moves very little and transfers weight from the trunk to the pelvis. Ankylosing spondylitis usually begins at this joint (sacroiliitis).

ar-1c090eed.stem: What type of joint is the pubic symphysis?
ar-1c090eed.explanation: The two pubic bones meet by surfaces covered with hyaline cartilage through an intervening fibrocartilaginous disc (interpubic disc). In pregnancy the ligaments loosen under hormonal influence and the joint widens slightly.

ar-fb65a359.stem: Which statement about the openings formed by the sacrospinous and sacrotuberous ligaments is true?
options: They separate the muscular and vascular lacunae.
They convert the greater and lesser sciatic notches into the greater and lesser sciatic foramina.
They form the floor of the inguinal canal.
They form the wall of the pudendal canal.
ar-fb65a359.explanation: These two ligaments bind the sacrum to the ischium and stop the sacrum tipping forwards. They convert the greater sciatic notch into the greater sciatic foramen and the lesser notch into the lesser sciatic foramen. Piriformis divides the greater sciatic foramen into suprapiriform and infrapiriform parts.

ar-081572fb.stem: Which of the following is NOT a feature of a synovial joint?
options: Bone ends fused together by fibrous tissue
ar-081572fb.explanation: In synovial joints the bone ends are covered with hyaline cartilage and separated by a joint cavity; the cavity is enclosed by the synovial membrane and fibrous capsule, and synovial fluid nourishes and lubricates it. Fusion by fibrous tissue is a feature of fibrous joints (sutures, syndesmoses).

options: Each joint is supplied by a single nerve
The nerves supplying the muscles that move a joint also supply that joint and the skin over it
Articular cartilage is rich in nerves
A joint's ligaments act opposite to its muscles
A joint's blood supply comes only from the capsular arteries
ar-faa2b7bc.explanation: Hilton's law explains why joint pain can be referred to distant areas: for example, because the obturator nerve also supplies the hip joint, hip disease can cause pain on the inner side of the knee. Articular cartilage has no nerves or vessels.

ar-35071863.stem: What type of joint attaches the teeth to their sockets?
ar-35071863.explanation: A gomphosis is a type of fibrous joint: the tooth root is pegged into its alveolar socket by the periodontal ligament. Sutures join skull bones, a syndesmosis the distal tibia and fibula; the epiphyseal plate is a synchondrosis, and the pubic symphysis and intervertebral discs are symphyses.

ar-471daa9c.stem: Which of the following is NOT a synchondrosis?
options: Joint between the 1st rib and manubrium
Y-shaped cartilage of the hip bone
ar-471daa9c.explanation: Synchondroses are primary cartilaginous joints formed by hyaline cartilage, and most ossify with time. The pubic symphysis is a secondary cartilaginous joint (symphysis) containing a fibrocartilage disc; the intervertebral discs and manubriosternal joint also belong to this group.

ar-78703f7e.stem: What movement mainly occurs at the atlanto-occipital joint?
options: Turning the head left and right (the 'no' movement)
Nodding the head forwards and backwards (the 'yes' movement)
ar-78703f7e.explanation: The occipital condyles sit on the superior articular facets of the atlas; this ellipsoid joint mainly allows flexion–extension and a little lateral bending. Most rotation occurs at the atlanto-axial joints.

ar-044f5001.stem: The nuchal ligament is the continuation in the neck of which ligament?
ar-044f5001.explanation: The supraspinous ligament, joining the tips of the spinous processes, broadens above C7 into the triangular nuchal ligament extending to the external occipital protuberance; it provides attachment for trapezius and splenius.

ar-06ded398.stem: The tectorial membrane is the upward continuation of which ligament?
ar-06ded398.explanation: The posterior longitudinal ligament broadens upwards from the body of the axis as the tectorial membrane and attaches to the clivus; it covers the dens and cruciform ligament from behind and protects the spinal cord.

ar-c597d8fc.stem: What are the components of the cruciform ligament of the atlas?
options: Transverse ligament of the atlas and longitudinal bands
Alar ligaments and apical ligament of the dens
ar-c597d8fc.explanation: The horizontal limb of the cruciform ligament is the transverse ligament of the atlas, holding the dens against the anterior arch; its vertical limbs are longitudinal fibres running from the body of the axis to the foramen magnum. The alar ligaments run from the sides of the dens to the occipital condyles and limit rotation.

ar-ed470bcc.stem: Before intubation, a patient with long-standing rheumatoid arthritis has flexion–extension neck X-rays; in flexion the distance between the atlas and dens increases markedly. Weakening of which ligament is chiefly responsible for this instability?
ar-ed470bcc.explanation: Rheumatoid synovitis erodes the ligaments around the dens; when the transverse ligament loosens, the atlas slides forwards in flexion and the dens can compress the spinal cord. This is why neck flexion is avoided during intubation in RA patients.

ar-f49987bc.stem: Which statement about the intervertebral disc is true?
options: There is also a disc between the atlas and axis
It makes up half the length of the spine
Its outer part is the fibrocartilaginous anulus fibrosus and its inner part the gelatinous nucleus pulposus
In adults the whole disc is well vascularised
ar-f49987bc.explanation: The discs are symphysis-type cartilaginous joints and make up about a quarter of the length of the spine. There is no disc between C1 and C2. In adults the disc is largely avascular and is nourished by diffusion from the end plates.
